title: Ownership and moves

spans.text: Goal: apply “Ownership and moves” to a real program or device. The key principle is: Non-
values such as String move, while

types such as integers are copied. Heap allocation alone does not determine which behavior applies. In a project, follow this guidance: After a move, the previous binding no longer owns the value; the compiler checks this.
QUESTION: What will this example do? Predict the result first.

Rust gives each value an owner, and resources are released when the owner leaves scope. Some values move; Copy values are duplicated cheaply.

Ownership means each value has one owner and its resource is released when that owner leaves scope. Moving a String with

values such as i32 are copied instead. The compiler checks this without a garbage collector.

Ownership determines which binding owns a non-
value and who releases its resources. Assigning a non-
value such as String moves it;
types such as integers can be copied. Heap allocation alone does not determine whether an assignment moves or copies. When supported,
values such as String move, while

types such as integers are copied. Heap allocation alone does not determine which behavior applies.

If omitted or changed: Ownership uses language rules instead of manual memory management or a garbage collector.
